title: Maturity Handling Schedule of Notice Days and Renewal Targets for Certificates of Deposit
content:
Each tier of the Certificates of Deposit line publishes when its maturity notice is mailed, whether it may renew automatically, the tier it renews into where the owner makes no change, and the basis on which the new rate is set.

| Tier | Maturity notice mailed, calendar days before maturity | Automatic renewal offered | Tier it renews into | Basis of the renewal rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | 20 | yes | 6-Month Certificate | the tier's standard rates published on the maturity date, plus any bonuses then earned |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | 20 | yes | 12-Month Certificate | the tier's standard rates published on the maturity date, plus any bonuses then earned |
| 12-Month Certificate | 20 | yes | 12-Month Certificate | the tier's standard rates published on the maturity date, plus any bonuses then earned |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | 30 | yes | 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | the tier's standard rates published on the maturity date, plus any bonuses then earned |
| 36-Month Certificate | 30 | yes | 36-Month Certificate | the tier's standard rates published on the maturity date, plus any bonuses then earned |
| 60-Month Certificate | 30 | yes | 60-Month Certificate | the tier's standard rates published on the maturity date, plus any bonuses then earned |

## Reading the schedule

Five tiers name themselves as their own renewal target. The 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate is the exception on this schedule: left to itself it renews into the 12-Month Certificate, so the tier of the new term is not the tier of the term that ended.

The notice column divides the line in two. The three shorter tiers give 20 days; the 18-Month Bump-Up, 36-Month and 60-Month Certificates give 30.
